questions.question: Historically, what shape was Earth once widely believed to have, alongside the belief that the Sun and stars revolved around it?
Until the 16th century, what did most people believe was located at the very centre of the universe?
By how many degrees is the axis on which the Earth spins tilted?
Why does the Northern Hemisphere experience summer in the month of June?
options: It is tilted towards the Sun
It is physically closer to the Sun in its orbit
The Sun produces more energy in June
The Southern Hemisphere blocks the cold winds

questions.question: How does the mass of an object affect the strength of its gravitational pull?
options: Greater mass results in weaker gravity
Greater mass results in stronger gravity
Mass does not affect gravity, only volume does
Mass only affects gravity if the object is spinning

questions.question: What happens to the gravitational force of a planet, moon, or star as you move further away from it into space?
options: It drops to zero immediately outside the atmosphere
It remains exactly the same strength

questions.question: What is the primary effect of the Earth's gravitational pull on the Moon?
options: It causes the Moon to spin faster on its axis
It continuously pulls the Moon closer until it crashes
It changes the Moon's direction, keeping it in orbit around the Earth
It heats up the core of the Moon through friction

questions.question: At which angle is heating a surface from a light or heat source the most effective?
What happens to rays of light when they strike a surface face-on compared to when they hit at an angle?
At what time of day is the heating effect of the Sun greatest at any given place on Earth?
Which of the following best describes a planet?
options: An extremely large sphere of hot gas that emits light
A small rocky fragment that orbits a moon
A very large sphere of rock or gas that orbits a star
A clump of ice and dust traveling between different galaxies

questions.question: How do the distances between objects in our solar system compare to the physical sizes of the objects themselves?
options: The distances are extremely small compared to the sizes of the objects
The distances are roughly equal to the diameters of the objects
The distances are very, very large compared to the sizes of the objects
The distances change so rapidly that they cannot be compared

questions.question: Why do countries near the Equator not experience distinct summer and winter seasons?
options: They stay close to 'face-on' to the Sun all year round
They are tilted away from the Sun during the entire year
They are much closer to the Sun than the polar regions
Their atmosphere blocks the Sun's rays more effectively

questions.question: What is a light-year, and why is it used by astronomers?
options: The time it takes for Earth to orbit the Sun, used to measure planetary ages
The distance light travels in one year, suitable for measuring vast space distances
The speed at which light travels through the vacuum of space
The brightness of a star compared to our Sun over a twelve-month period
